items.name: monoidal category (recalled)
items.statement_summary: A monoidal category M is a category with a bifunctor (tensor) box : M x M -> M, a natural isomorphism associator alpha : a(bc) ~= (ab)c, a unit object e, and natural isomorphism unitors lambda : ea ~= a and rho : ae ~= a, subject to the pentagon coherence axiom for alpha and the triangle axiom relating alpha, lambda, rho (with lambda = rho : ee -> e). Restated here from Chapter VII.1 as the base notion of the chapter.

items.name: braiding for a monoidal category
items.statement_summary: A braiding on a monoidal category M is a family of natural isomorphisms gamma_{a,b} : a box b ~= b box a satisfying (i) unit compatibility lambda o gamma_{a,e} = rho : a box e -> a, and (ii) both hexagon identities relating gamma to the associator alpha: one expressing gamma_{a box b, c} in terms of gamma_{a,c} and gamma_{b,c}, the other expressing gamma_{a, b box c} in terms of gamma_{a,b} and gamma_{a,c}. The braiding is NOT required to be involutive.

items.name: inverse of a braiding is a braiding
items.statement_summary: If gamma is a braiding on M then the pointwise-inverse family gamma^{-1} is again a braiding on M. Concretely, the first hexagon identity for gamma is equivalent to the second hexagon identity for gamma^{-1}, and conversely, so the hexagon axioms are preserved under inversion.

items.name: symmetric monoidal category (via braiding)
items.statement_summary: A symmetric monoidal category is a monoidal category equipped with a braiding gamma that is a symmetry: gamma_{b,a} o gamma_{a,b} = id_{a box b} for all a,b (i.e. gamma is self-inverse, gamma^2 = 1). Under this symmetry condition each of the two braiding hexagons implies the other. Same notion as defined in Chapter VII.7.

items.name: permuted-word functor (w tau)_M
items.statement_summary: For a symmetric monoidal category M, each box-word w in n letters (words as in VII.2) together with a permutation tau in the symmetric group S_n determines a functor (w tau)_M : M^n -> M given by (w tau)_M(a_1,...,a_n) = w(a_{tau 1},...,a_{tau n}), i.e. the word w evaluated on the tau-permuted argument list.

items.name: canonical maps / coherence for symmetric monoidal categories
items.statement_summary: In every symmetric monoidal category M there is a function assigning to each ordered pair (v sigma, w tau) of permuted words of the same length n a UNIQUE natural isomorphism can_M(v sigma, w tau) : (v sigma)_M => (w tau)_M of functors M^n -> M, the canonical map, characterized by: the identity of M and every instance of the associator alpha and the braiding gamma are canonical, and both the composite and the box-tensor of two canonical maps are canonical. Consequently any two such canonical (formal) maps between the same permuted words are equal (symmetric-monoidal coherence). An informal extension involving the unitors lambda, rho is noted and left to the reader.

items.name: monoidal (lax) functor
items.statement_summary: A monoidal functor (F, F_2, F_0) : M -> M' between monoidal categories consists of an ordinary functor F : M -> M', a natural transformation F_2(a,b) : F(a) box F(b) -> F(a box b), and a morphism F_0 : e' -> F(e), such that three coherence diagrams commute in M': an associativity/hexagon diagram relating F_2 to the associators alpha, alpha', and two unit diagrams relating F_2 and F_0 to the unitors lambda, rho and lambda', rho'. This is the lax monoidal functor (comparison maps not assumed invertible).

items.name: monoidal functors compose
items.statement_summary: The (evident) composite of two monoidal functors is again a monoidal functor; monoidal functors are closed under composition (with composite comparison maps built from those of the factors).

items.name: strong / strict monoidal functor
items.statement_summary: A monoidal functor (F, F_2, F_0) is STRONG when F_0 and every comparison F_2(a,b) are isomorphisms, and STRICT when F_0 and every F_2(a,b) are identities. (Recalled alongside: a monoidal category is strict when alpha, lambda, rho are all identities.)

items.name: monoidal natural transformation
items.statement_summary: A monoidal natural transformation theta : (F, F_2, F_0) => (G, G_2, G_0) : M -> M' between monoidal functors is an ordinary natural transformation theta : F => G whose components satisfy two coherence squares: G_2(a,b) o (theta_a box theta_b) = theta_{a box b} o F_2(a,b) (compatibility with the tensor comparison) and theta_e o F_0 = G_0 (compatibility with the unit comparison).

items.name: monoidal natural transformations compose
items.statement_summary: The (evident) composite of two monoidal natural transformations is again a monoidal natural transformation; monoidal natural transformations are closed under (vertical) composition.

items.name: word-indexed comparison transformation F_v
items.statement_summary: For a monoidal functor F and each tensor box-word v in n letters (words as in VII.2), there is a natural transformation F_v : v(F a_1,...,F a_n) -> F(v(a_1,...,a_n)) with F_box = F_2 and F_e = F_0, defined inductively by F_{v box v'} = F_2 o (F_v box F_{v'}). All resulting coherence diagrams commute; for a word-comparison eta : v => w built from alpha, rho, lambda the square relating F_v, F_w, eta commutes, and for a monoidal natural transformation theta : F => G the square relating F_v, G_v, theta commutes - generalizing the monoidal-functor axioms (3),(4) and the monoidal-transformation axioms (5),(6).

items.name: braided monoidal functor
items.statement_summary: For braided (or symmetric) monoidal categories B, B' with braidings gamma, gamma', a braided monoidal functor is a monoidal functor (F, F_2, F_0) : B -> B' compatible with the braidings: F(gamma_{a,b}) o F_2(a,b) = F_2(b,a) o gamma'_{F a, F b}. These are the morphisms of the category of braided monoidal categories.

items.name: strict monoidal category (recalled)
items.statement_summary: A monoidal category is strict when its structure isomorphisms - the associator alpha and the unitors lambda, rho - are all identities; equivalently the tensor is strictly associative and e is a strict two-sided unit. Recalled from Chapter VII.1 (printed parenthetical on p.257 has a scan-ambiguous middle letter; p.256 states it unambiguously as alpha, lambda, rho).

items.name: strictification: every monoidal category is equivalent to a strict one
items.statement_summary: Every monoidal category M is categorically equivalent to a strict monoidal category S, the equivalence realized by strong monoidal functors G : M -> S and F : S -> M. In the proof S is the free monoid on the objects of M (finite strings of objects under concatenation, empty string the unit; alpha, lambda, rho identities), F sends a string to the left-parenthesized (front-associated) tensor of its entries and G sends b to the one-element string [b], with F G = id_M and G F naturally isomorphic to id_S.

items.name: coherence for associativity from strictification
items.statement_summary: If a monoidal category M is equivalent, via a strong monoidal functor G : M -> S, to a strict monoidal category S, then coherence for the associativity of the tensor (and likewise for the unit isomorphisms rho, lambda) holds in M: any two natural transformations built from alpha (resp. rho, lambda) between the same pair of tensor-word functors are equal. Proof transports parallel canonical maps through the equivalence, where strictness of S collapses them to equality.

items.name: endofunctor category is strict monoidal
items.statement_summary: Show that for any category C the endofunctor category C^C, with composition of endofunctors as the tensor product and the identity functor 1_C as the unit, is a strict monoidal category.

items.name: strong monoidal functor T : M -> M^M
items.statement_summary: For C = M a monoidal category (Exercise 1), exhibit a strong monoidal functor T = (T, T_2, T_0) : M -> M^M into the strict monoidal endofunctor category, with T(a) = a (tensor) -, coherence map T_2(a,b) given componentwise by the associator alpha_{a,b,c}, and unit map (T_0)_a = lambda(a)^{-1}; verify that the monoidal-functor axioms (3),(4) for T reduce to axioms (5),(7),(9) of the monoidal-category definition in section VII.1.

items.name: independent proof of strictification and coherence
items.statement_summary: Using Exercises 1-2, give a proof of the strictification theorem (Theorem 1 of XI.3: every monoidal category is monoidally equivalent to a strict monoidal category) that is independent of the coherence theorem, thereby also obtaining an independent proof of coherence via Theorem 2.

items.name: the Artin braid group B_n
items.statement_summary: Defines a braid on n strings (taken up to continuous deformation) with multiplication by concatenation/stacking, an identity and inverses; the resulting group is the Artin braid group B_n, presented by generators sigma_1,...,sigma_{n-1} subject to sigma_i sigma_{i+1} sigma_i = sigma_{i+1} sigma_i sigma_{i+1} and sigma_i sigma_j = sigma_j sigma_i for |i-j| =/= 1. Equivalently B_n is the fundamental group of the configuration space T_n of n distinct points in the plane. Special cases: B_3, B_2 infinite cyclic on sigma_1, B_1 trivial.

items.name: surjective homomorphism B_n -> S_n
items.statement_summary: The map sending each braid on n strings to the permutation it induces on its n endpoints is a surjective group homomorphism B_n -> S_n onto the symmetric group, given on generators by sigma_i |-> tau_i = (i, i+1); it is the quotient that adjoins sigma_i^2 = 1. Records the standard presentation of S_n by transpositions tau_i with relations tau_i^2 = 1, tau_i tau_j = tau_j tau_i for |i-j| =/= 1, and tau_i tau_{i+1} tau_i = tau_{i+1} tau_i tau_{i+1}.

items.name: the braid category B
items.statement_summary: Assembles all braid groups into the braid category B: objects are the natural numbers 0,1,2,...; hom(n,n) = B_n with no arrows between distinct objects. Under the tensor box = + (sum on objects, side-by-side juxtaposition of braids) with unit the object 0 / empty braid, B is a strict monoidal category.

items.name: the braiding gamma_{m,n} on B
items.statement_summary: On the braid category B the family gamma_{m,n} : m+n -> n+m that crosses the block of m strings over the block of n strings is a braiding: a transformation natural in m and n satisfying both hexagon identities, making B a braided monoidal category. It is NOT a symmetry: the symmetry law gamma^2 = 1 fails.

items.name: canonical automorphisms of a tensor and the action of B_2
items.statement_summary: In a braided monoidal category, unlike the symmetric case, the 'canonical' automorphisms of a two-fold tensor a box b need not collapse to the identity: the maps 1, gamma^2, gamma^{-2}, gamma^4, gamma^{-4}, ... : a box b -> a box b furnish infinitely many, so a subgroup of the braid group B_2 acts on a box b and not all diagrams built from the braiding gamma commute.

items.name: braid category is the free braided monoidal category on one object
items.statement_summary: For B the braid category and any braided monoidal category M with underlying ordinary category M_0, evaluation at the object 1 of B is an equivalence of categories hom_BMC(B, M) ~= M_0, where hom_BMC(B, M) is the category of strong braided monoidal functors B -> M with their monoidal natural transformations. (I.e. B is the free braided monoidal category on one generating object; Joyal-Street.) Proof strictifies M, then for each object a builds a strict braided monoidal functor F_a with F_a(1) = a, F_a(n) = a^n, F_a(sigma_i) = 1^{i-1} box gamma_{a,a} box 1^{n-i-1}, checks the braid relations via the two hexagons, and shows evaluation at 1 is full, faithful, essentially surjective.

items.name: braided coherence via underlying braid
items.statement_summary: Every composite of the canonical maps (those built from the associator alpha, unit isomorphisms lambda, rho, and braiding gamma) acting on an n-fold tensor product in a braided monoidal category M has a well-defined underlying element of the braid group B_n. Two such composites are equal in every braided monoidal category M if and only if they determine the same element of B_n. This is the braided-coherence theorem (Joyal-Street): coherence holds as classification of composites by their underlying braid, not as 'all diagrams commute'.
